openclaw_frozen_test_control.scope: independent frozen-test postmortem; original failed acceptance unchanged

retained_client_limits: Vulkan Gemma 31B at 8192 stopped before API/client tasks because model diagnostics returned not_ready; no agent pass counted
ROCm Gemma 31B at 8192 with OpenCode 2.2.6 passed cart but timed out rate limiter and Python after repeated reads/tests without edits; protected files remained intact
ROCm Qwen 3.5 9B OpenClaw rewrote the protected test file; its independently passing pristine-test control does not erase the failed original task

excluded_probe.reason: initial operator-host test used integrated graphics because host and dedicated container GPU indices differ; owned processes stopped; replacement preflights explicitly verify gfx1201

scope_limits: Linux x86_64 Vulkan on R9700 and Intel Xe2, and ROCm on R9700; certified candidate is unpublished
Release-policy contexts: 2048 for the starter, 4096 for larger models; actual-client AMD campaigns use one slot at 16384, except Gemma 31B at 8192
Gemma 31B ROCm supplementary client trials use ZINC_PREFILL_CHUNK=128 and default F32 KV; this does not expand default-path 4096-token qualification
Current actual-client cohort uses the documented OpenCode 2.0.21 pin; the separate 2.2.6 failures and all earlier failed trials remain visible
Starter inference checks do not qualify the 0.6B model for coding or agent tasks
Model task-delivery failures remain failures; neither a successful client exit nor a separate control replaces independent tests and protected-file checks
Bounded client fixtures do not establish universal coding quality or long-running soak stability
Supplementary actual-client campaigns run on AMD; Intel certification covers the selected inference/API profile rather than this client matrix
Premerge preview controls are diagnostic evidence at their own archive/source identities, separate from the final-version candidate
F32/Q8 premerge diagnostic size checks do not qualify optional inference configurations; the API control uses default Vulkan F16
Native memory reports remain conservative estimates, including lazy scratch/JIT/cache caveats; actual requests separately test allocation and inference
No new latest-llama.cpp throughput or all-dimension performance claim
Metal remains an unsigned preview; CUDA and native Intel remain outside the stable Linux promise
